Found the bug. In the debug section case:

```c
if (internal_ptr->u.syment._n._n_n._n_offset > debug_sec->size   // note: > not >=
    || debug_sec_data + offset < debug_sec_data)
  ... "<corrupt>"
else
  _n_offset = debug_sec_data + offset;
```

So if offset == debug_sec->size, the symbol name points to `debug_sec_data + size`, which is exactly one past the end of the allocated buffer (allocated with `_bfd_alloc_and_read (abfd, sec_size, sec_size)` — which allocates exactly sec_size bytes, no null terminator appended). Then when printing the symbol name (e.g., in the error message "unrecognized storage class ... `%s'"), it reads off the end of the heap buffer → heap buffer overflow (read).

Also if offset == size, the name points to one-past-end and reading it is out of bounds.
